questions.stem: A student was asked to find the mass of salt dissolved in $ 1 0 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of sea water. She was given the following instructions. Step A Weigh an empty evaporating basin Step B Transfer 50 $ cm^{3} $ of sea water into the basin Step C Heat the sea water in the basin until all the water has evaporated Step D Allow the basin and residue to cool Step E Weigh the basin and residue of salt

parts.label: a
parts.text: During the experiment, the student used several pieces of apparatus. Some of them are shown in the table. Complete the table.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State, with a reason, one safety precaution that the student should take when doing this experiment. Precaution Reason

questions.stem: The diagrams show the reactions of some metals with cold water and with dilute hydrochloric acid. Metals in cold water Metals in dilute hydrochloric acid

parts.label: a
parts.text: Answer the following questions, using only the metals that appear in the diagrams.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Name two metals that react with cold water.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Name one metal that reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid but not with cold water.

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: Arrange the five metals in order of reactivity.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Some magnesium powder is added to dilute sulfuric acid in a test tube. A colourless solution is formed and a gas is given off. When more magnesium is added, the reaction continues for a while and then stops, leaving some magnesium powder in the test tube. When a flame is placed at the mouth of the test tube, the gas burns with a squeaky pop.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Identify the gas produced.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Suggest why the reaction stops.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: State the name of the colourless solution.

parts.label: b-iv
parts.text: How could you separate the magnesium powder from the colourless solution?

parts.label: c
parts.text: In some fireworks, magnesium powder reacts quickly with oxygen in the air. During this reaction heat energy is produced.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: What name is given to reactions in which heat energy is produced?

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Name the compound formed when magnesium reacts with oxygen.

questions.stem: When solutions are mixed together, precipitates sometimes form.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Barium carbonate is an insoluble compound. It is formed as a precipitate when solutions of the soluble compounds barium chloride and sodium carbonate are mixed. When solutions of the soluble compounds potassium chloride and sodium sulfate are mixed, no precipitate is formed. Complete the table to show the results of mixing solutions of some compounds.

parts.label: b
parts.text: When solutions of lead(II) nitrate and potassium bromide are mixed, a precipitate of lead(II) bromide and a solution of potassium nitrate are produced. $\mathrm {P b} \left(\mathrm {N O} _ {3}\right) _ {2} (\dots \dots \dots \dots) + 2 \mathrm {K B r} (\dots \dots \dots \dots) \rightarrow \mathrm {P b B r} _ {2} (\dots \dots \dots \dots) + 2 \mathrm {K N O} _ {3} (\dots \dots \dots \dots)$ The equation for the reaction is Complete the equation by inserting the state symbols.

parts.label: c
parts.text: In order to prepare a pure, dry sample of lead(II) bromide, a student took the mixture produced in part (b). He then filtered the mixture washed the solid residue with distilled water left the solid in a warm place for several hours

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Why did the student filter the mixture?

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Why did he wash the solid residue?

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: Why is it better to use distilled water rather than tap water to wash the solid residue?

parts.label: c-iv
parts.text: Why did he leave the solid in a warm place?

questions.stem: The apparatus in the diagram is used to collect the oxygen produced by the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide, $ \mathrm{H_{2}O_{2}} $

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a chemical equation for the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe a test to show that the gas collected in the syringe is oxygen.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Manganese(IV) oxide is a catalyst for this reaction. State and explain the effect of a catalyst on the rate of this reaction.

questions.stem: The element carbon has three common isotopes. These are carbon-12, carbon-13 and carbon-14.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the table to show the number of protons and neutrons in each isotope of carbon.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain, in terms of electrons, why the three isotopes have the same chemical properties.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State what is meant by the term relative atomic mass, $ A_{r} $

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: A sample of carbon contained 98.90% carbon-12 and 1.10% carbon-13. Use this information to calculate the relative atomic mass of carbon in the sample. Give your answer to two decimal places. Relative atomic mass

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why decane is described as a hydrocarbon.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Give the molecular formula for decane.

parts.label: b

parts.label: c

questions.stem: When ammonia gas and hydrogen chloride gas mix, they react together to form a white solid called ammonium chloride. The equation for the reaction is: $\mathrm {N H} _ {3} (\mathrm {g}) + \mathrm {H C l} (\mathrm {g}) \rightarrow \mathrm {N H} _ {4} \mathrm {C l} (\mathrm {s})$ After five minutes, a white ring of solid ammonium chloride formed. A cotton wool pad was soaked in ammonia solution and another was soaked in hydrogen chloride solution. The two pads were then put into opposite ends of a dry glass tube at the same time.

parts.label: a
parts.text: What name is given to the movement of the two gases?

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Identify which gas is moving faster and give a reason for your choice.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The experiment was repeated at a higher temperature. State and explain how this change would affect the time taken for the white ring to form.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Gas particles move at a speed of several hundred metres per second at room temperature. Suggest one reason why it took five minutes for the white ring to form.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b

parts.label: b-i

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Explain, in terms of its bonding and structure, why silicon dioxide has a very high melting point.

parts.label: a-i

parts.label: a-ii

parts.label: b

parts.label: b-ii

parts.label: b-iii

questions.stem: Lead can be extracted from lead(II) sulfide, PbS, in two stages. Stage 1: Lead(II) sulfide is heated in air. It reacts with oxygen to produce lead(II) oxide and sulfur dioxide. Stage 2: The lead(II) oxide is then heated in a blast furnace with coke.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a chemical equation for the reaction in Stage 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The equation for the reaction that occurs when lead(II) oxide is heated with coke in a blast furnace is: $2 \mathrm {P b O} + \mathrm {C} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {P b} + \mathrm {C O} _ {2}$

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: State, with a reason, whether PbO is oxidised or reduced in this reaction.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Calculate the minimum mass, in tonnes, of coke needed to react with 44.6 tonnes of lead(II) oxide. $ [ 1 \mathrm{t o n n e}=1 0^{6} \mathrm{g} ] $

parts.label: c
parts.text: The molten lead obtained from the blast furnace contains 0.1% silver dissolved as an impurity. The silver is removed by: adding zinc to the mixture of molten lead and silver at 530 $ ^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ and removing the mixture of molten zinc and silver that forms on top of the molten lead heating the mixture of molten zinc and silver until the zinc boils off as a gas, leaving almost pure, solid silver behind Use the information above to answer the following questions.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: What can you deduce about the relative solubility of silver in zinc and in lead?

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: What can you deduce about the melting point of the mixture of zinc and silver?

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: What can you deduce about the boiling point of zinc compared to that of silver? Explain your answer.

parts.label: c-iv
parts.text: Suggest why so much trouble is taken to remove such a small amount of silver from the lead.

questions.stem: (a) Crystals of hydrated zinc sulfate, $ \mathrm{Z n S O_{4}. x H_{2} O} $ , contain water of crystallisation. He weighed the empty tube A. He placed a sample of hydrated zinc sulfate crystals in tube A and reweighed it. He heated the tube, allowed it to cool and weighed it again. He repeated this process until two consecutive masses were the same. This is known as 'heating to constant mass'. When hydrated zinc sulfate crystals are heated gently, they decompose according to the following equation: $\mathrm {Z n S O} _ {4}. \mathrm {x H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} \rightarrow \mathrm {Z n S O} _ {4} + \mathrm {x H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$ The following masses were recorded: $\mathrm {M a s s o f t u b e A} = 1 0. 1 2 \mathrm {g}$ $\mathrm {M a s s o f t u b e A} + \mathrm {Z n S O} _ {4}. \mathrm {x H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} = 1 8. 7 3 \mathrm {g}$ Mass of tube A and $ \mathrm{Z n S O_{4}} $ after heating to constant mass = 14.95 g (i) Calculate the mass of $ \mathrm{Z n S O}_{4} $ formed after heating to constant mass. (ii) Calculate the mass of water collected after heating to constant mass. (iii) The relative formula mass of $ \mathrm{Z n S O_{4}} $ is 161 The relative formula mass of water is 18 Use this information, and your answers to (a)(i) and (a)(ii), to calculate the value of x in the formula $ \mathrm{Z n S O_{4}. x H_{2}O} $ Show your working. A student used the apparatus shown to remove and collect the water of crystallisation from the crystals in order to find the value of x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Why is it necessary to heat the crystals to constant mass?

parts.label: c
parts.text: Describe how the student could use a chemical test to show that the liquid collected was water.
